Subject: Re: Acme reference request — proposal: standby/on-call pool + capacity gating

Team —

Recap: Acme (Lisa) has a hard blackout for June. Ben flagged procurement pressure from Jordan to get a reference call prior to that. Given our current cadence, Acme has been fielding a lot of requests (we track ~8 requests in last 90 days). That's causing measurable reference fatigue.

Proposal (quick):
- Create a 4-person standby/on-call pool for mid-market PLG accounts that can be pinged for short calls (20–30m). Pool members rotate weekly.
- Gate requests by priority: procurement > analyst briefings > sales discovery. If procurement is urgent, escalate to the pool.
- Offer recorded testimonials or written Q&A as a lower-friction alternative (we get better acceptance).
- Maintain a 14–30 day rest window per customer between asks; exceptions require CS approval.

I'm attaching the current availability export (reference_availability_v2.csv) and an initial standby_terms doc. Please review and comment with names you recommend for the standby rotation and any blackout rules to add. We need a short policy for Ben to present to Jordan tomorrow.

Attachments: reference_availability_v2.csv, standby_pool_terms.docx

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme reference request — standby pool nominations + cadence

+1 on the pool idea. Quick suggestions:

Candidates for initial 4-person standby pool (volunteers & heavy refs):
- Rafael Mendes (Customer, willing to do short calls) — external
- Grace O'Connor (Customer) — external
- Marcus Lin (ops) — internal support for scheduling
- Ben Carter (AE) — handle procurement escalations

Rotation cadence: weekly on-call owner, 30-minute slots reserved Tue/Thu mornings.

Blackout rules: 30-day rest after a live reference; limit live requests to 2 per quarter unless customer explicitly opts in. Procurement requests get priority but must be validated via the deal owner. For blackout periods (like Acme's June launch) we offer: recorded video + brief written FAQ + a named substitute.

Script idea for recorded option is attached. If Acme is open to a 10–12 minute recorded testimonial + 5-question FAQ we can mark this as low-friction and avoid exhausting Acme.

Attachments: script-outline.pdf

-Marissa
Senior Customer Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Quick question on Acme availability for reference requests

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for working with Jordan on the procurement review. Ben flagged that they were hoping for a short customer reference call prior to June. I completely understand your product launch blackout (6/1–6/30) — congrats on the launch, by the way.

Two options that would keep this light on your team:
1) A 10–12 minute recorded testimonial (we record over Zoom, we edit it down, you approve) + short written FAQ answers (5 questions).
2) A single 20–30 minute live call before 6/1 (we can be flexible on times).

If neither works, would you be open to us introducing a short-call substitute peer (someone from our standby pool) who can speak to implementation/scale rather than launch-specifics? We will not share private data and will only connect your team if agreed.

No problem either way — just want to avoid pinging you during the blackout. Appreciate a quick note on what you'd prefer.

Best,
Marcus
Head of GTM Ops, Redwood Inference

Marcus —

Thanks for the heads-up and for being considerate about our launch window. To be clear: we will not be doing live reference calls between 6/1 and 6/30. We also want to limit outside calls the two weeks leading into launch (so from 5/18 onward it's already tight).

What works for us: a short recorded testimonial (we can do a 10–12 minute recorded segment and answer 4–5 high-level questions). We prefer Redwood to handle the recording and editing.

We are open to a live 30-minute call the week of July 19 (after our post-launch retros), but nothing earlier. Also you may provide a substitute peer — fine to connect to them as long as they are not used as our primary quote in any public-facing materials.

Lisa Wang
